title: minthostachys mollis var. mandoniana
intro: Minthostachys mollis var. mandoniana, commonly known as Mandon's mint, is a plant species in the Lamiaceae family, traditionally used in Andean folk medicine. The health benefits of Mandon's mint include its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which are attributed to its ability to alleviate digestive issues, reduce fever, and soothe respiratory problems. The therapeutic actions of this plant are primarily due to its bioactive constituents, such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which exhibit antispasmodic, anti-anaphylactic, and vasodilatory effects. Studies have identified the bioactive constituents of Mandon's mint as including flavonoids like rutin, quercetin, and kaempferol, as well as phenolic acids like ferulic acid and caffeic acid.
